newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar slips to another 8-year low close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar slips to another 8-year low close.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar continued its slow but steady depreciation on Thursday to end at yet another eight-year low, reflecting persistent quarter-end need for the U.S. dollars by importers, dealers said.
The local unit closed at T$27.920 against Wednesday's T$27.909 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a modest US$169 million.
The Taiwan dollar struggled in an extremely narrow T$27.910-924 range throughout the session due to what dealers suspected was intervention orchestrated by the central bank.
Thursday's closing marked the lowest level since a T$28.03 finish on January 7, 1989.
"Active demand for the U.S. dollar shows no signs of fading, but the market can clearly feel the central bank's attempt to smooth the fall," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said the central bank was determined to intervene and blunt the local currency's recent slide.
"T$27.95 should be the near-term support for the Taiwan dollar," the dealer said.
The Taiwan dollar's recent depreciation has been in line with the average forecast of six senior Taipei dealers in an informal May 30 Reuters Poll.

Four of the dealers said Taiwan's easing dollar would break eight-year support at T$28 in the third quarter, citing slack economic growth and political uncertainties -- but not before the central bank put up a strong defence to slow the slide.
Two dissenting dealers acknowledged the depreciation pressure, but said the central bank would mount a defence of such vigour that the currency would remain above T$28.
